attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own newsletter post. He endorses them as his description of the post-GPT-5 climate.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps 'seemed' as 'has appeared' and does not turn it into a measured increase. It is an observation about the past, framed as an impression, with no period or measure.

contract.note: The contract fairly treats 'seemed' as a qualified impression. Requiring a measured rise in the share of industry financing would add a commitment the speaker did not make. Any decisive test would depend on reading in a measure and a comparison period.

reviews.rationale: This is a qualified impression ('seemed'). It names no measure, baseline or industry boundary, so no fair test can confirm or refute it without making it a stronger claim. The evidence packet is empty because no search was run, and the stated gaps say this is not a finding either way. Not adjudicable.
